evidenceRule: No acceptance status advances solely because documentation or simulated tests pass.

evidenceLevels.requiredEvidence: Working hosted Supervisor and verified runtime behavior

acceptedArchitecture: Supervisor to A2A Investigation Planner. Step D installer writes a JSON catalog and one hosted VM specialist. Observability specialist planned.

steps.title: Discovery & reconciliation
steps.value: Read-only inventory reconciles the approved JAWS DEV resources without changing cloud state.
steps.evidence: DEV reconciliation remains the accepted evidence. Installer 0.4.10 Discover supports an empty subscription and offline Pester passed. A fresh-subscription discovery receipt has not been recorded, so greenfield Step A is not accepted.

steps.title: Foundry foundation & packaging
steps.value: An approved plan can create a Foundry account, project, model deployment, Key Vault, registry, project identity pull role, and a digest-pinned hosted Supervisor.
steps.evidence: Code and offline CLI-stand-in tests cover Preflight, Install, and Accept. Provisioning, functional acceptance, and customer installation are not recorded. The plan digest binds names and model, not an unbounded cost.

steps.title: Supervisor → Investigation Planner
steps.value: Supervisor v5 returns a completed, read-only VM diagnostic plan through an identity-protected A2A prompt planner.
steps.evidence: Closed DEV: Supervisor v5, planner v1, TASK_STATE_COMPLETED; hosted investigation runtime did not execute. Install-JawsThroughStepC.ps1 -EnvironmentName reads a Step B receipt and offline Pester covers that path. A fresh-subscription functional receipt has not been recorded, so the Step B path is not accepted.

steps.title: Virtual-machine specialist & compute
steps.capability: JSON specialist catalog and VM compute
steps.value: A hosted VM specialist owns one compute environment. The catalog refuses an unknown tool, a phase agent, a second sandbox, and a write without the approval workflow.
steps.evidence: The installer writes the JSON catalog and, outside the dev project, creates one hosted virtual-machine specialist from the Step B image. The dev project binds jaws-investigation-dev and does not post a second agent. Offline Pester covers the catalog refusals and a CLI stand-in. The Supervisor image is not changed to load the catalog. No fresh-subscription receipt is recorded, so Step D is not accepted.

steps.title: Azure MCP investigation
steps.value: The VM specialist loads an investigation skill and returns cited evidence through an allow-list of Azure MCP tools for that machine.
steps.evidence: Target capability; not implemented or accepted.

steps.title: Deliberation & remediation
steps.value: The same VM specialist compares options in a skill. A workflow checks identity, RBAC, and human approval before one write tool runs.
steps.evidence: Target capability; not implemented or accepted.

steps.title: Observability specialist & custom MCP
steps.value: One prompt observability specialist uses shared compute. Datadog, Azure Monitor, Sentinel, and ServiceNow incident tools are compiled modules named by a JSON manifest.
steps.evidence: Target capability; not implemented or accepted.

steps.title: Teams projects & conversations
steps.value: A Teams conversation stores the thread. A project record stores the incident, decisions, approvals, and citations. Personal preferences stay with that operator.
steps.evidence: Target capability; not implemented or accepted.

steps.title: End-to-end operational acceptance
steps.value: A Teams-originated VM security incident uses both specialists, one compute environment, and their allow-lists. A second conversation in the project can name the incident, the last decision, and the last citation.
steps.evidence: Target capability; not implemented or accepted.
